note: E12 (Brad, the one-off deep-question scenario). Each item is a candidate correspondence whose SURFACE (matching label + kind) is genuinely insufficient to decide -- the label is the same on both sides, so it could be a true correspondence or a false cognate. Exactly ONE requestable attribute disambiguates it; the others are shared or uninformative. The test is whether the agent RECOGNISES the shortfall and issues a TARGETED request for the disambiguating attribute (distinct from running the whole decisive experiment / asking for everything), then decides correctly. 'requestable' is the menu of attribute names the agent may ask for (available on both sides); 'facts' are the values, revealed only when requested; 'disambiguating' is the single attribute that resolves the item; 'gold_corresponds' is the truth.

a.function: a layer-2 broadcast domain (a customer VLAN)

b.function: a multi-homing link bundle identified by an ESI

items.why: same label 'segment' and same layer (ethernet), but function differs: a broadcast domain vs a multi-homing link bundle -- the classic false cognate. Only 'function' separates them.

a.quantity: one-way propagation delay of the circuit

b.quantity: one-way propagation delay of the circuit

items.why: both denote the same quantity (one-way circuit delay); 'role' differs (measured vs required) but does not change the referent. 'quantity' confirms the correspondence.
same label 'grade', same tier_count (3) and assignable_by (operator), but they govern different things (optical protection vs IP scheduling). Only 'governs' separates them.

a.intent: survive a failure of the path

b.intent: survive a failure of the path

items.why: both denote the same intent (survive a path failure) over the same scope; 'mechanism' differs (realise vs require) but not the referent. 'intent' confirms the correspondence.

a.role: the service access point at one attachment

b.role: the service access point at one attachment

items.why: both are the per-attachment service access point; 'named_per' differs only in local naming (UNI vs AC). 'role' confirms the correspondence.
